title: Work IQ: federated connectors for governed access to more data sources
summary: Pass: the roadmap facts, connector licensing and documented controls are supported, and the briefing distinguishes existing controls from unconfirmed Work IQ applicability. One minor qualification remains: the general OAuth description should acknowledge that custom connectors also support unauthenticated sources.

claims.claim: Work IQ is planned to use federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.
claims.quote: Enable Work IQ to use federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Graph", "Work IQ"]

claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Existing federated connectors require a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7 for querying users, supporting the add-on classification.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether this roadmap capability changes existing federated connector licence requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "federated" "licensing". Read connector prerequisites, Work IQ API overview, Work IQ overview and Foundry Work IQ licensing prerequisites; no roadmap-specific change to federated connector licence requirements is stated.

claims.claim: The medium cost rating rests on the documented add-on licensing for users querying existing federated connectors, not a claimed new Work IQ meter.
claims.quote: A Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license for every user who queries the federated source.

claims.claim: Federated Copilot connectors use Model Context Protocol.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors retrieve data from external systems in real time.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use MCP to access data in real time, so Copilot can retrieve up-to-date information directly from external systems.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors access data using the user's identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Admins manage and govern existing federated connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: How this roadmap capability surfaces federated connectors in Work IQ is not described in detail.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "federated connectors" launch available connectors. Read roadmap, federated connectors overview and Work IQ overview; search excerpts describe federated data generally but not this roadmap capability's detailed Work IQ experience.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The source system enforces the user's permissions for federated connector access and changes.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.claim: The federated connector model does not copy external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors don't copy or store data in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Retrieved connector data is used in conversational responses.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.claim: Federated connectors use OAuth 2.0.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.
claims.fix: Remove 'Uses OAuth 2.0 and' from the bullet and retain 'Uses the user's permissions in the source system.' The cited overview supports OAuth, but https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/set-up-custom-federated-connectors also lists 'No Auth' with 'Users don't need to authenticate.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can create, update or delete source data with user approval.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval.

claims.claim: New write-capable connector tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: Federated connectors remain read-only in the Researcher agent.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.claim: The general Copilot connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only, unlike the detailed overview's write-action documentation.
claims.quote: Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: MCP server firewalls may need to allow Microsoft's static egress IP addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Work IQ API use has usage-based billing using Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The preview Foundry Work IQ guidance says connector-backed tools can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for each calling user.
claims.quote: Confirm the selected connector's prerequisites. A connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user.

claims.claim: The separate Work IQ API and Foundry guidance does not establish a billing rule specifically for roadmap item 570670.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "federated" "licensing". Opened Work IQ API overview, Work IQ overview and Foundry Work IQ prerequisites: they distinguish API consumption and connector-specific licensing, without identifying this roadmap capability's integration or charging path.

claims.claim: Existing connector enable, disable and staging controls are under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > connector.
claims.quote:
| Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections | Turns an individual connector on or pauses it without removing configuration. |
| Staged rollout | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > Staged rollout |

claims.claim: Tenant-level Work IQ MCP policy can be turned on or off under Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools.
In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP.
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP Policy tab is shown when available rather than guaranteed in every tenant.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for turning Work IQ MCP policy on or off is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" API tenant settings; "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "graph.microsoft.com". Opened Policy governance for Work IQ MCP; results and page describe policy concepts and the admin UI but no callable policy-toggle endpoint.

claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "federated connectors" controls policy availability; "Work IQ" "federated connectors" default licensing admin controls. Opened connector management, Work IQ overview, Work IQ MCP policy and Package Management API overview; no feature-specific control found.
